claim: When no SurrogateType is given, the change always serializes T in contractless mode, even if T carries MessagePack or DataContract attributes. Attributes on T are never read: [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract] and [DataMember] are all ignored. The requirement says that if T does carry MessagePack attributes they are honoured, and that contractless applies only when T has no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject]. Consequences: an [IgnoreMember] public property on T is still serialized; [Key(int)] array layouts become string-keyed maps; a public property without [DataMember] on a [DataContract] type is still serialized. The wire format then disagrees with what T's own attributes (and the dynamic resolver) produce.

claim: The formatted type's own MessagePack attributes are ignored, which breaks an acceptance criterion. With no surrogate, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`, which takes every public read-write member with a string key and never reads `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]` or `[IgnoreMember]` on T. Example: T is `[MessagePackObject] class MyType { [Key(0)] int Value; [IgnoreMember] string Secret; }`. The generated formatter writes a string-keyed map and serializes `Secret`, although T's attributes require an int-keyed array without `Secret`. This changes the wire format compared with T's declared contract. Ledger L18 says to follow the requirement, and the requirement says 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.'

claim: The interface-count guard is too broad. It only rejects `formatterInterfaces.Length == 0`, but MsgPack020's message says the formatter must implement IMessagePackFormatter<T> for exactly one data type. Example: `partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<A>, IMessagePackFormatter<B>`. No MsgPack020 is reported, and the generator silently picks `formatterInterfaces[0]` in AllInterfaces order. The user gets CS0535 for the other interface instead of the intended diagnostic. The same happens when a base class already implements another IMessagePackFormatter<X>, because AllInterfaces includes inherited interfaces.

claim: The contractless key order is alphabetical (OrderBy Name) and the formatter uses string keys. The wire format may therefore differ from ContractlessStandardResolver, which serializes members in declaration order. Users who switch from the dynamic contractless resolver to this generated formatter would see different map key order. The bytes also change if members are later reordered or renamed. Members lacking a public setter are also skipped here, whereas ContractlessStandardResolver serializes get-only properties and readonly fields.

claim: Surrogate mode with int keys hands intKey values to CreateMember directly. For sparse keys (for example 0 and 5) the generated array formatter needs gap handling. Gaps are not checked here. The result may be a crash, or the wrong array length.

claim: The model is built with nestedFormatterRequired: false and no formatters are produced for member types. A public member of T whose type is another attribute-less type from Project A (e.g. ProjectA.Address) has no formatter in Project B's source-generated resolver, so serializing T throws at run time. The requirement asks for contractless behaviour over public members, and contractless resolution in MessagePack normally recurses into member types. The README lists this as a limitation, but the requirement does not.
